# Non-occupational:

Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) for Exposure to Blood or Body Fluids for HIV (sexual, injection drug use, or other substantial non-occupational HIV exposure)

# Please review and follow the Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) Protocol:
< SELECT HERE > Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Non-occup Protocol
Assessment for nPEP:
A case-by-case determination about nPEP is recommended when the HIV status of the source of the body fluids is unknown and the reported exposure presents a substantial risk for transmission if the source did have HIV infection.
Eligibility for nPEP requires BOTH:

1. Less than 72 hours since exposure < AND >
2. High-risk anatomic site of exposure < AND >

(vagina, rectum, eye, mouth or other mucous membrane, nonintact skin, percutaneous inoculation)

3. High-risk type of fluid < AND >

(blood, semen, vaginal secretions, rectal secretions, breast milk, any body fluid visibly contaminated with blood)

4.  Known (or strongly suspected) HIV-positive source

When source HIV status is unknown, recommend erring on the side of providing antivirals for nPEP given the safety and tolerability of these medications, while including the patient in shared decision making.

2\. High risk for acquisition (all three factors below)

Assess for three key risk factors, all three must be present for an exposure to qualify as high risk:

1\. High-risk anatomic site of exposure < AND > a. Vagina b. Rectum c. Eye d. Mouth or other mucous membrane e. Nonintact skin f. Percutaneous inoculation
2\. High-risk type of fluid < AND > a. Blood b. Semen c. Vaginal secretions d. Rectal secretions e. Breast milk f. Any body fluid visibly contaminated with blood
3\. Known (or strongly suspected) HIV-positive source
